correctness.rationale: On a strictly ordered finite product with positive normalized product masses, centered coordinate regressors are pairwise orthogonal and have positive variances. The coefficient along each coordinate is a weighted covariance divided by variance. Discrete summation by parts with zero-sum centered coordinate coefficients yields positive prefixes U and an exact decomposition into fiber edge differences. Triangle inequality bounds all output edge variation by the maximum of B_j U_jk/(s_j^2 w_jk) times input variation. Each candidate sharp ratio is realized by a single product-axis step, which has no other-direction differences. For uniform sites, exact sums U_k=k(n-k)/(2n), s^2=(n^2-1)/12, B=n-1 give max 6 floor(n^2/4)/(n(n+1)), equivalently 3 floor(n/2)/(2floor(n/2)+1). The small-dimension threshold and limiting envelope follow algebraically. The bundled independent direct projector and cut enumeration verifies eight rational cases, but only the analytical proof covers all weights and dimensions.

value.rationale: The exact all-factor theorem classifies a natural mixed norm of multivariate regression for every strictly positive product sampling law and arbitrary positive anisotropic factorized edge weights, reducing potentially exponentially large grid calculations to linear cost in axis sizes. It identifies the first instability dimension and all finite uniform plateaus, and distinguishes stability of Boolean cube regression in edge variation from positivity preservation. These are a natural completed classification and useful boundaries for signal smoothing and approximation stability, without asserting statistical consequences.
